name: Cloud
description: The minimal-agent cloud connector. It owns the network transport to the cloud backend and registers that transport in the host transport registry. Thus the Intercom peers and teams span machines, and Intercom does not import this plugin. Skeleton: the remote transport is a stub (no live connection) until the backend auth contract lands. Tool: CloudStatus.

tool.name: CloudStatus
tool.description: Show the status of the minimal-agent cloud plugin. The tool shows if the cloud functions are on, the cloud flags, and if the network transport is in the registry. Each use also adds the transport (a placeholder) to the registry, one time only. For example, `CloudStatus({})`.

format.description: The output format. The default is `text`.

tool.name: CloudLogin
tool.description: Log this CLI in to the minimal-agent cloud backend with the OAuth device flow (RFC 8628). The tool shows a user code and a URL for approval in a browser. Then it saves the access token on this computer. After the login, teleport, and peers and teams on other computers start. To set the backend, set `MINIMAL_AGENT_CLOUD_URL` (default `http://localhost:4000/api/auth`). For example, `CloudLogin({})`.

tool.name: CloudPush
tool.description: Upload the new records of this session to the cloud teleport store immediately. Then the user can see the session live on the web or a mobile device. The tool sends only the records that the cloud does not have, thus you can use it again safely. It operates only after `CloudLogin` and when the cloud functions are on. The upload also starts automatically between turns. For example, `CloudPush({})`.
